advice.msg: an effectful array callback needs an inline arrow so its world transitions are read in array order
advice.do: [conditional: the function has no `this`, `arguments` or `new.target` in it and is never called with `new`] The callback must be an arrow function with plain parameters. A named function is read by name when its own parameters are plain; otherwise pass it the arguments JavaScript passes, `xs.map((x, i, a) => f(x, i, a))`, or only the ones it reads. An effectful callback may destructure its element or default it where the element type never holds undefined; name the fields you read instead of a rest element.

advice.msg: TS2345: Argument of type 'Function' is not assignable to parameter of type '(value: string, index: number, array: string[]) => string'.   Type 'Function' provides no match for the signature '(value: string, index: number, array: string[]): string'.
advice.do: [migration] A type error under strict mode; the proof needs the types to hold.
